P2400.title: EVAP Leak Detection Pump Control Circuit Open
P2400.description: The control circuit to the EVAP leak-detection pump is open. Without that pump the ECU cannot pressurise the fuel-vapour system to test for leaks.

causes.label: Pin pushed back out of connector body

symptoms: Possible smell of fuel near tank or engine bay

P2401.title: EVAP Leak Detection Pump Control Circuit Low
P2401.description: Drive voltage on the leak-detection pump line is below the lower limit. Often a short to ground in the harness.

causes.label: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

symptoms: Possible smell of fuel near tank or engine bay

P2402.title: EVAP Leak Detection Pump Control Circuit High
P2402.description: Drive voltage on the leak-detection pump line is above the upper limit. Usually a short to supply or open ground.

causes.label: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

symptoms: Possible smell of fuel near tank or engine bay

P2403.title: EVAP System Leak Detection Pump Sense Circuit Open
P2403.description: The leak detection pump (LDP) - which actively pressurises the EVAP system to find leaks - has an open sense circuit. The ECU cannot read the pump status during the diagnostic cycle.

causes.label: Open in pump or sense wiring
Pin pushed back out of connector body
Cracked solder joint inside the module or sensor

symptoms: Possible smell of fuel near tank or engine bay

P2404.title: EVAP Leak Detection Pump Sense Circuit Range/Performance
P2404.description: The sense (reed-switch or current-feedback) signal from the leak-detection pump is electrically valid but does not match expectations during a leak test. Often a worn pump diaphragm or a sticking reed contact.

causes.label: Sensor element aged beyond calibration window

symptoms: Possible smell of fuel near tank or engine bay

P2405.title: EVAP System Leak Detection Pump Sense Circuit Low
P2405.description: Same as P2403 with the sense voltage below the plausible range. The evaporative system captures fuel vapor from the tank and purges it into intake; leaks or stuck purge valves leak hydrocarbons and cause emissions failures.

causes.label: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

symptoms: Possible smell of fuel near tank or engine bay

P2406.title: EVAP System Leak Detection Pump Sense Circuit High
P2406.description: Same as P2403 with the sense voltage above the plausible range. The evaporative system captures fuel vapor from the tank and purges it into intake; leaks or stuck purge valves leak hydrocarbons and cause emissions failures.

causes.label: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
Supply wire pinched against B+ source

symptoms: Possible smell of fuel near tank or engine bay

P2407.title: EVAP Leak Detection Pump Sense Circuit Range/Performance
P2407.description: The leak detection pump returns a sense signal that is electrically valid but does not match the expected response during the pump's self-test or pressure cycle.

causes.label: Sensor element aged beyond calibration window

symptoms: Possible smell of fuel near tank or engine bay

P2408.title: Fuel Cap Sensor/Switch Circuit Range/Performance
P2408.description: On vehicles with a sensed fuel cap, the cap-status signal is electrically valid but does not change as expected when the cap is opened or closed.

causes.label: Cap seal aged, switch never seats
Sensor element aged beyond calibration window

P2409.title: Fuel Cap Sensor or Switch Circuit Range or Performance
P2409.description: The sensor or switch that detects whether the fuel cap is properly closed reports a value within plausible range yet not matching driver action.

P240A.title: EVAP System Leak Detection Pump Heater Control Circuit Open
P240A.description: The leak detection pump heater - keeps the pump diaphragm warm in cold weather - has an open control circuit.

causes.label: Pin pushed back out of connector body
Cracked solder joint inside the module or sensor

symptoms: Possible smell of fuel near tank or engine bay

P240B.title: EVAP System Leak Detection Pump Heater Control Circuit Low
P240B.description: Same as P240A with the control line shorted to ground. The leak detection pump, often called the DMTL module on European cars, pressurises the EVAP system to test it for leaks; newer pumps have a heater in the housing that dries out moisture and stops ice from seizing the pump in cold weather. With the heater circuit faulty the leak test may be skipped or give false results in winter; engine running is not affected.

causes.label: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

symptoms: EVAP leak test does not complete in cold weather (readiness monitor not set)

P240C.title: EVAP System Leak Detection Pump Heater Control Circuit High
P240C.description: Same as P240A with the control line shorted to supply. The leak detection pump, often called the DMTL module on European cars, pressurises the EVAP system to test it for leaks; newer pumps have a heater in the housing that dries out moisture and stops ice from seizing the pump in cold weather. With the heater circuit faulty the leak test may be skipped or give false results in winter; engine running is not affected.

causes.label: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
Supply wire pinched against B+ source

symptoms: EVAP leak test does not complete in cold weather (readiness monitor not set)

P240D.title: Alternative Fuel Low Pressure System Leak
P240D.description: The control module has detected a leak on the low-pressure side of the alternative fuel system, the part downstream of the pressure regulator that feeds gas to the fuel rail. On GM's bi-fuel Impala, for example, the regulator brings CNG down from tank pressure to about 470–900 kPa. Monitors usually infer a leak from pressure that falls while the shut-off valves are closed, or from rail pressure that cannot be held. Bi-fuel systems then close the gas valves and continue on gasoline. Natural gas and LPG are flammable, so the lines, fittings and regulator should be checked for leaks before the gas mode is used again.

causes.label: Leaking pressure regulator, low-pressure shut-off valve or injector seal
Pressure sensor drift faking a pressure loss

symptoms: Check engine or alternative fuel warning light on
Gas mode unavailable, engine runs on gasoline only
Gas smell near the tank, lines or engine bay

P240E.title: Alternative Fuel High Pressure System Leak
P240E.description: The control module has detected a leak on the high-pressure side of the alternative fuel system, between the tank and the pressure regulator, where CNG is stored at up to about 25 MPa (3,600 psi). This section includes the tank valves, the high-pressure lines and filter and the inlet of the regulator. Monitors usually infer a leak from tank or line pressure that drops while no gas is being used. Bi-fuel systems then close the tank solenoid valves and continue on gasoline. Because of the stored pressure and the flammable gas, the system should be checked by a qualified shop before the gas mode is used again.

causes.label: Hose, fitting or cylinder valve leak
Pressure sensor drift faking a pressure loss

symptoms: Check engine or alternative fuel warning light on
Gas mode unavailable, engine runs on gasoline only
Gas smell near the tank, lines or engine bay

P240F.title: EGR Slow Response
P240F.description: The EGR system reacts to commanded changes more slowly than calibrated - typically a partly clogged EGR cooler, sticky valve, or worn actuator.

P2410.title: Fuel Cap Sensor/Switch Stuck
P2410.description: The fuel cap status switch is stuck in one position — the ECU never sees the expected transition between open and closed.

P2411.title: Fuel Cap Sensor/Switch Circuit
P2411.description: A general electrical fault on the fuel cap sensor/switch circuit — open or short.

P2412.title: Fuel Cap Sensor or Switch Circuit Intermittent or Erratic
P2412.description: Same as P2409 with intermittent or erratic signal. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.

causes.label: Connector with intermittent contact under vibration

P2413.title: Exhaust Gas Recirculation System Performance
P2413.description: The ECU monitors EGR flow indirectly through MAF, MAP or differential-pressure feedback and finds that actual EGR flow does not match the commanded value over a sustained period.

P2414.title: O2 Sensor Exhaust Sample Error Bank 1 Sensor 1
P2414.description: Same as P237A but on the upstream sensor B1S1 (pre-catalyst). A drifted or sluggish lambda sensor lets the mixture run lean or rich without correction — fuel economy and emissions suffer immediately.

P2415.title: O2 Sensor Exhaust Sample Error (Bank 2 Sensor 1)
P2415.description: P2415 indicates that the upstream air-fuel sensor on bank 2 is not reading a representative exhaust sample - typically because outside air is drawn in through a leak near the sensor or the sensor is not seated correctly, so the reading is implausibly lean. VW's 2014 specification books for the Passat, CC and Touareg evaluate the sensor signal voltage against two bands, 3.70-4.81 V and a lower band of 2.51-3.00 V or 3.0-3.70 V, the band being switched with the gain factor used for the sensor characteristic. P2414 is the identical check on bank 1. CARB requires fuel-control sensors to be monitored for every parameter that affects emissions. Expect a warning light and possibly rough running and higher consumption.

causes.label: Exhaust leak ahead of or near the sensor (manifold, gasket, flex pipe)

symptoms: Ticking exhaust noise when a leak is present
Higher fuel consumption or uneven running

P2416.title: O2 Sensor Signals Swapped (Bank 1 Sensor 2 / Bank 1 Sensor 3)
P2416.description: P2416 means the engine computer concludes that the two downstream oxygen sensors of bank 1 - sensor 2 after the first catalyst and sensor 3 after a second catalyst, as used mainly on SULEV/PZEV vehicles - are connected the wrong way round. No manufacturer publicly documents the detection logic for P2416. By analogy with P0040, which VW sets when the lambda controllers of the two front sensors move beyond their limits in opposite directions, the check compares the expected and actual response of each sensor. The usual cause is swapped connectors after a sensor replacement or harness repair. CARB requires secondary oxygen sensors to be monitored for proper function. P2417 is the bank 2 counterpart, P0041 a swap between banks.

causes.label: Sensor 2 and sensor 3 connectors swapped after a repair
Wrong sensor type or harness length fitted in one position
Wires crossed in a harness repair

symptoms: Check engine light shortly after an exhaust or sensor repair
Catalyst monitor not completing or giving implausible results

P2417.title: O2 Sensor Signals Swapped (Bank 2 Sensor 2 / Bank 2 Sensor 3)
P2417.description: P2417 is set when the engine computer finds that the two downstream oxygen sensors on bank 2 - sensor 2 behind the first catalyst and sensor 3 behind a second one - respond as if their wiring were exchanged. Such three-sensor layouts are typical of V-engines built to SULEV/PZEV limits. No manufacturer publicly documents the detection logic for P2417; the closest documented analogue is P0040, which VW sets when two sensors drive their lambda controllers past opposite limits. In practice the fault follows a repair in which plugs or harness branches were mixed up. CARB requires secondary oxygen sensors to be checked for proper function. P2416 is the same check on bank 1, P0041 a swap between the banks.

causes.label: Sensor 2 and sensor 3 connectors swapped after a repair
Wrong sensor type or harness length fitted in one position
Wires crossed in a harness repair

symptoms: Check engine light shortly after an exhaust or sensor repair
Catalyst monitor for bank 2 not completing

P2418.title: EVAP System Switching Valve Control Circuit/Open
P2418.description: P2418 is the electrical check of the control circuit of the EVAP switching valve - an extra valve in the evaporative system whose job depends on the design. Ford calls it EVAP switching valve or vapor blocking valve; its 2012 and 2020-2023 OBD summaries check the driver continuously and set P2418 when a short, open or intermittent fault persists for more than 5 s, so at Ford this one code covers all circuit faults. Karma's Revero and GS-6 bulletin uses P2418 for the open control circuit of the rear fuel tank isolation valve driven by the ECM. P2419/P2420 separate low and high circuit faults, P2450 is the mechanical stuck-open fault. While the valve cannot be controlled, leak tests are suspended and fuel vapour odour or refuelling trouble may follow.

causes.label: Broken control wire or unplugged valve connector
Open solenoid coil in the switching valve
Corroded connector near the tank (road salt, splash water)

symptoms: Possible fuel vapour odour or slow refuelling

P2419.title: EVAP System Switching Valve Control Circuit Low
P2419.description: P2419 reports that the control circuit of the EVAP switching valve reads low - usually the control line is shorted to ground, or the driver stage measures too little voltage. Karma's Revero/GS-6 bulletin lists P2419 for the rear fuel tank isolation valve controlled by the ECM. Subaru's bulletin 09-103-23 for 2015 Legacy and Outback with an evaporative leak check module (ELCM) tells technicians to look for P2419 and P2420 whenever the ELCM pump fault P2404 is stored, because the switching valve sits in the same module. Ford, by contrast, reports every circuit fault of this valve as P2418. CARB requires output components to be checked for circuit faults. P2420 is the high-side fault, P2418 the open circuit. The leak test is suspended and the warning light comes on.

causes.label: Control wire shorted to ground (chafed near tank or frame)
Shorted coil in the switching valve or leak check module
Water ingress into the leak check module

symptoms: Often stored together with leak detection pump codes

P241A.title: O2 Sensor Signals Swapped Bank 1 Sensor 1 and Sensor 2
P241A.description: The pre- and post-catalyst lambda signals on bank 1 are swapped - the upstream sensor responds like a downstream sensor and vice versa. Typically the harness was reversed during a sensor change.

P241B.title: O2 Sensor Signals Swapped Bank 2 Sensor 1 and Sensor 2
P241B.description: The pre- and post-catalyst lambda signals on bank 2 are swapped - the upstream sensor responds like a downstream sensor and vice versa. Typically the harness was reversed during a sensor change.

P241C.title: Throttle Actuator Control System Ice Blockage Bank 2
P241C.description: The throttle actuator on bank 2 cannot move because of ice formation - typical for very cold ambient temperature with humid intake. Engine de-ices on warm-up.
symptoms: Reduced throttle response, possible limp mode
Idle too high or too low

P241D.title: SCR Inducement Forced Engine Shutdown
P241D.description: The SCR inducement strategy (mandatory regulatory measure to enforce AdBlue refilling and emissions compliance) has reached the final stage and shut down the engine. Refill AdBlue and clear inducement fault to restart.

causes.label: AdBlue tank empty or out of compliance

symptoms: Check engine light or NOx warning on
Possible no-start countdown after ignore period

P241E.title: Reductant Heater Coolant Control Valve Stuck Closed
P241E.description: The valve that routes engine coolant to heat the AdBlue lines is stuck closed - AdBlue lines do not warm up and may freeze in cold weather, blocking dosing.

causes.label: Carbon or debris buildup preventing free movement
Component wear with age - mechanical play

symptoms: Check engine light or NOx warning on
Possible no-start countdown after ignore period

P241F.title: EGR Cooler B Efficiency Below Threshold
P241F.description: The temperature drop across EGR cooler B is below the calibrated threshold - cooler is fouled with soot, has internal scaling, or coolant flow is restricted. Recirculated gas reaches the intake hotter than designed, increasing NOx and combustion temperatures.

causes.label: Cooler fouled with soot or scaled

P2420.title: EVAP System Switching Valve Control Circuit High
P2420.description: P2420 means the control circuit of the EVAP switching valve reads high - typically a short to battery voltage on the control line or an overcurrent detected by the driver stage. Karma lists P2420 for the rear fuel tank isolation valve of the Revero and GS-6, which the ECM operates, and Subaru's bulletin 09-103-23 for 2015 Legacy/Outback with an evaporative leak check module (ELCM) includes P2420 among the codes to check alongside the pump fault P2404. Ford instead reports all circuit faults of its switching valve as P2418. CARB requires output components to be monitored for circuit faults. P2419 is the low-side fault and P2418 the open circuit. The evap leak monitor cannot run until the circuit is repaired.

causes.label: Control wire shorted to battery voltage
Switching valve coil with too low resistance (overcurrent)
Faulty driver stage in the ECM

P2421.title: EVAP Vent Valve Stuck Open
P2421.description: The evaporative emission system vent valve does not close on command. The ECU detects that the evap system cannot hold pressure or vacuum because the canister is permanently vented to atmosphere.

causes.label: Carbon or debris buildup preventing free movement

symptoms: Possible smell of fuel near tank or engine bay

P2422.title: EVAP Canister Vent Valve Stuck Closed
P2422.description: The vent valve at the canister end of the EVAP system cannot open. Without ambient air entering the canister, fresh fuel cannot purge the stored vapors and refueling may trigger ORVR issues. Common with rusted or rodent-damaged vent valves.

causes.label: Carbon or debris buildup preventing free movement

symptoms: Possible smell of fuel near tank or engine bay

P2423.title: HC Adsorption Catalyst Efficiency Below Threshold Bank 1
P2423.description: The ECU determines that the hydrocarbon adsorption catalyst on bank 1 no longer holds enough HC during cold start to meet emission targets. Often due to ageing or thermal damage.
symptoms: Sulfur (rotten egg) smell from exhaust under load

P2424.title: HC Adsorption Catalyst Efficiency Below Threshold Bank 2
P2424.description: The hydrocarbon adsorption catalyst on bank 2 - which traps HC during cold-start until the main catalyst lights off - is degraded; HC slip during cold start is above the calibrated threshold.
symptoms: Sulfur (rotten egg) smell from exhaust under load

P2425.title: EGR Cooling Valve Control Circuit Open
P2425.description: The valve that admits coolant flow to the EGR cooler has an open control circuit - cooling cannot be enabled and EGR temperatures stay too high.

causes.label: Pin pushed back out of connector body
Cracked solder joint inside the module or sensor

P2426.title: EGR Cooling Valve Control Circuit Low
P2426.description: Same as P2425 with the control line shorted to ground. EGR mixes inert exhaust into intake to lower combustion peak temperature — too little raises NOx, too much causes misfires and rough running.

causes.label: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P2427.title: EGR Cooling Valve Control Circuit High
P2427.description: Same as P2425 with the control line shorted to supply. EGR mixes inert exhaust into intake to lower combustion peak temperature — too little raises NOx, too much causes misfires and rough running.

causes.label: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
Supply wire pinched against B+ source

P2428.title: Exhaust Gas Temperature Too High Bank 1
P2428.description: An EGT sensor on bank 1 reports a temperature above the safety threshold for prolonged operation - typical for blocked DPF, restricted exhaust, or excessive fuelling. Risk of catalyst, DPF or turbo damage.

P2429.title: Exhaust Gas Temperature Too High Bank 2
P2429.description: An EGT sensor on bank 2 reports a temperature above the safety threshold for prolonged operation - typical for blocked DPF, restricted exhaust, or excessive fuelling. Risk of catalyst, DPF or turbo damage.

P242A.title: Exhaust Gas Temperature Sensor Circuit Bank 1 Sensor 3
P242A.description: A general circuit fault is detected on the EGT sensor at bank 1 sensor 3 (typically just downstream of the turbo or before the catalyst). The ECU loses thermal protection feedback for the catalyst and DPF.

P242B.title: Exhaust Gas Temperature Sensor Circuit Range or Performance Bank 1 Sensor 3
P242B.description: Same as P242A with the signal in plausible range yet not matching the engine model.

P242C.title: Exhaust Gas Temperature Sensor Circuit Low Bank 1 Sensor 3
P242C.description: Same as P242A with the signal voltage below the plausible range. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.

causes.label: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P242D.title: Exhaust Gas Temperature Sensor Circuit High Bank 1 Sensor 3
P242D.description: Same as P242A with the signal voltage above the plausible range. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.

causes.label: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
Supply wire pinched against B+ source

P242E.title: Exhaust Gas Temperature Sensor Circuit Intermittent or Erratic Bank 1 Sensor 3
P242E.description: Same as P242A with intermittent or erratic signal. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.

causes.label: Connector with intermittent contact under vibration

P242F.title: Particulate Filter Restriction Ash Accumulation Bank 1
P242F.description: The diesel particulate filter on bank 1 reports backpressure attributable to ash (non-combustible residue from oil and fuel additives, not removable by regeneration). The filter has reached the end of its service life and needs cleaning or replacement.
symptoms: Check engine light or DPF warning light on

P2430.title: AIR System Air Flow or Pressure Sensor Circuit Bank 1
P2430.description: A general circuit fault on the secondary air injection (AIR) system flow or pressure sensor on bank 1 - the sensor that verifies air pump flow during cold-start enrichment compensation.

P2431.title: Secondary Air Injection System Air Flow/Pressure Sensor Circuit
P2431.description: The ECU detects a general fault in the secondary air injection system air flow or pressure sensor circuit. The diagnostic cannot verify proper SAI operation.

P2432.title: Secondary Air Injection System Air Flow/Pressure Sensor Circuit Range/Performance
P2432.description: The signal of the SAI air flow or pressure sensor is implausible during operation. The reading does not change as expected when the air pump is commanded.

causes.label: Sensor element aged beyond calibration window

P2433.title: AIR System Air Flow or Pressure Sensor Circuit High Bank 1
P2433.description: Same as P2430 with the signal voltage above the plausible range. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.

causes.label: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
Supply wire pinched against B+ source

P2434.title: AIR System Air Flow or Pressure Sensor Circuit Intermittent or Erratic Bank 1
P2434.description: Same as P2430 with intermittent or erratic signal. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.

causes.label: Connector with intermittent contact under vibration

P2435.title: AIR System Air Flow or Pressure Sensor Circuit Bank 2
P2435.description: AIR System Air Flow or Pressure Sensor Circuit Bank 2: an electrical fault is present in the circuit.

P2436.title: AIR System Air Flow or Pressure Sensor Circuit Range or Performance Bank 2
P2436.description: Same as P2430 on bank 2 with the signal in plausible range yet not matching the engine model.

P2437.title: AIR System Air Flow or Pressure Sensor Circuit Low Bank 2
P2437.description: AIR System Air Flow or Pressure Sensor Circuit Low Bank 2: the signal voltage is below the expected range. Often a short to ground or high resistance in the wiring.

causes.label: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P2438.title: AIR System Air Flow or Pressure Sensor Circuit High Bank 2
P2438.description: Same as P2433 on bank 2. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.

causes.label: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
Supply wire pinched against B+ source

P2439.title: AIR System Air Flow or Pressure Sensor Circuit Intermittent or Erratic Bank 2
P2439.description: Same as P2434 on bank 2. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.

causes.label: Connector with intermittent contact under vibration

P243A.title: Particulate Filter Restriction Ash Accumulation Bank 2
P243A.description: The diesel particulate filter on bank 2 reports backpressure attributable to ash (non-combustible residue from oil and fuel additives, not removable by regeneration). The filter has reached the end of its service life and needs cleaning or replacement.
symptoms: Check engine light or DPF warning light on

P243B.title: Particulate Filter Restriction Forced Limited Power Bank 2
P243B.description: Particulate Filter Restriction Forced Limited Power Bank 2: the control module has detected this fault condition.
symptoms: Check engine light or DPF warning light on

P243C.title: Particulate Filter Regeneration Frequency Bank 2
P243C.description: The DPF on bank 2 needs regeneration more often than calibrated. Possible causes are an oil-burning engine, fuel-injector leak, short-trip operation, or a sensor offset.
symptoms: Check engine light or DPF warning light on

P243D.title: Particulate Filter Regeneration Duration Bank 2
P243D.description: Regenerations on bank 2 take longer than calibrated to complete - typically a low EGT during the cycle (cold weather, short trips) or a partially aged catalyst before the DPF.
symptoms: Check engine light or DPF warning light on

P243E.title: Particulate Filter Regeneration Incomplete Bank 2
P243E.description: Particulate Filter Regeneration Incomplete Bank 2: the control module has detected this fault condition.
symptoms: Check engine light or DPF warning light on

P243F.title: Particulate Filter Restriction Soot Accumulation Too High Bank 2
P243F.description: Particulate Filter Restriction Soot Accumulation Too High Bank 2: the control module has detected this fault condition.
symptoms: Check engine light or DPF warning light on

P2440.title: Secondary Air Injection System Switching Valve Stuck Open (Bank 1)
P2440.description: The switching/check valve in the secondary air injection plumbing on bank 1 is stuck in the open position. With the valve permanently open, exhaust gas can back-feed into the air pump and corrode it, while the downstream O2 sensor sees ambient air constantly.

causes.label: Switching valve stuck open by carbon or corrosion
Carbon or debris buildup preventing free movement
Component wear with age - mechanical play

P2441.title: Secondary Air Injection System Switching Valve Stuck Closed (Bank 1)
P2441.description: The switching valve on bank 1 will not open when commanded, so no secondary air reaches the exhaust during cold start. Catalyst light-off is delayed and emissions during the cold-start window rise.

causes.label: Switching valve stuck closed by carbon
Carbon or debris buildup preventing free movement

P2442.title: Secondary Air Injection System Switching Valve Stuck Open (Bank 2)
P2442.description: The switching/check valve in the secondary air injection plumbing on bank 2 is stuck in the open position. With the valve permanently open, exhaust gas can back-feed into the air pump and corrode it, while the downstream O2 sensor sees ambient air constantly.

causes.label: Carbon or debris buildup preventing free movement
Component wear with age - mechanical play

P2443.title: Secondary Air Injection System Switching Valve Stuck Closed (Bank 2)
P2443.description: The switching valve on bank 2 will not open when commanded, so no secondary air reaches the exhaust during cold start. Catalyst light-off is delayed and emissions during the cold-start window rise.

causes.label: Carbon or debris buildup preventing free movement
Component wear with age - mechanical play

P2444.title: Secondary Air Injection System Pump Stuck Off (Bank 1)
P2444.description: The secondary-air pump does not run when commanded during cold start. Often a seized pump (after exhaust back-feed corroded the impeller), a blown fuse, or a failed relay.

P2445.title: Secondary Air Injection System Pump Stuck On (Bank 1)
P2445.description: The secondary-air pump continues to run after the cold-start window, when the ECU has commanded it off. Usually a stuck-closed relay welding the pump permanently to battery voltage.

causes.label: Carbon or debris buildup preventing free movement

P2446.title: Secondary Air Injection Pump Stuck Off (Bank 2)
P2446.description: Bank 2 secondary air pump does not deliver air when commanded. The catalyst light-off process is delayed and cold-start emissions rise.

causes.label: Carbon or debris buildup preventing free movement

P2447.title: Secondary Air Injection Pump Stuck On (Bank 2)
P2447.description: Bank 2 secondary air pump runs continuously. Either a stuck-on relay or a shorted control output keeps the pump powered when it should be off.

causes.label: Carbon or debris buildup preventing free movement

P2448.title: AIR System High Air Flow Bank 1
P2448.description: The secondary air injection system on bank 1 delivers more flow than calibrated when the pump is commanded on - typically a stuck-open switching valve allowing free flow.

P2449.title: AIR System High Air Flow Bank 2
P2449.description: The secondary air injection system on bank 2 delivers more flow than calibrated when the pump is commanded on - typically a stuck-open switching valve allowing free flow.

P244A.title: Diesel Particulate Filter Differential Pressure Too Low
P244A.description: The differential pressure across the DPF is below the calibrated minimum even at higher loads. Often a sign of a damaged or missing filter substrate, or a leak in the sensing line.
symptoms: Check engine light or DPF warning light on

P244B.title: Diesel Particulate Filter Differential Pressure Sensor Offset
P244B.description: At engine off, the DPF differential pressure sensor does not return to zero within the allowed offset window. The static offset is too large to be ignored.
symptoms: Check engine light or DPF warning light on

P244C.title: Exhaust Temperature Too Low For Particulate Filter Regeneration Bank 1
P244C.description: During an attempted regeneration of the bank 1 DPF the EGT did not reach the temperature window needed for soot oxidation. Regeneration could not start or was held. Driving in higher load is needed.

causes.label: Engine load too low for regeneration

symptoms: Check engine light or DPF warning light on

P244D.title: Exhaust Temperature Too High For Particulate Filter Regeneration Bank 1
P244D.description: Same as P244C with the EGT too high - regeneration paused to protect filter substrate from melt damage.

causes.label: Engine load too high - filter overheating risk

symptoms: Check engine light or DPF warning light on

P244E.title: Exhaust Temperature Too Low For Particulate Filter Regeneration Bank 2
P244E.description: During an attempted regeneration of the bank 2 DPF the EGT did not reach the temperature window needed for soot oxidation. Regeneration could not start or was held. Driving in higher load is needed.

causes.label: Engine load too low for regeneration

symptoms: Check engine light or DPF warning light on

P244F.title: Exhaust Temperature Too High For Particulate Filter Regeneration Bank 2

causes.label: Engine load too high - filter overheating risk

symptoms: Check engine light or DPF warning light on

P2450.title: EVAP System Switching Valve Performance/Stuck
P2450.description: The EVAP switching valve does not respond to commands as expected. The valve is mechanically stuck or unable to switch between purge and vent paths, blocking proper leak diagnosis.
symptoms: Possible smell of fuel near tank or engine bay

P2451.title: EVAP System Switching Valve Stuck Closed
P2451.description: The EVAP switching valve - which directs vapor flow between purge and leak-detection paths - is stuck in the closed position. The diagnostic cycle cannot complete.

causes.label: Carbon or debris buildup preventing free movement
Component wear with age - mechanical play

symptoms: Possible smell of fuel near tank or engine bay

P2452.title: Diesel Particulate Filter Pressure Sensor A Circuit
P2452.description: The pressure sensor A of the particulate filter, usually a differential sensor with hoses to the filter inlet and outlet, tells the ECM how loaded the filter is. Despite its generic circuit title, P2452 is in practice an offset check made when no exhaust flows. Ford's 2023 diesels run it in after-run and set the code when the sensor still reads more than 1 kPa. GM's 2018 diesels check the filter inlet pressure at the start of the drive cycle, after at least 10 s engine off, and set it as a Type B code when the offset is too big. A sensor that has drifted, moisture inside it or a hose holding pressure all give such an offset. Audi saw P2452 together with P2453, P2454, P2456 and P2002 on the 2009 to 2011 Q7 TDI and traced it to moisture entering the differential pressure sensor G505 through poor internal sealing; the fix was a sensor with better sealing. The soot model then works with wrong values, so regeneration timing suffers.

causes.label: Sensor offset drifted or moisture inside the sensor
Sensor hose blocked by soot or condensate

symptoms: Regeneration too early, too late or inhibited

P2453.title: Diesel Particulate Filter Pressure Sensor A Circuit Range/Performance
P2453.description: P2453 means the particulate filter pressure signal is electrically fine but does not behave like a real filter pressure. Manufacturers use two kinds of test. With the engine off there should be almost no pressure difference: GM's 2009 Duramax fails above 4.1 kPa, the 2014 Cruze 2.0 diesel above 3.2 kPa in after-run, and the Opel/GM 2.0 CDTi in the Saab 9-5 (2010) checks once at least 60 s after shutdown. With the engine running the signal has to follow changes in exhaust flow: the Duramax expects it to rise and fall when the flow changes by more than 200 m³/h per second, and Ford's 2023 diesels fail a reading under 1 kPa at 500 m³/h or more, which points to a disconnected or split hose. Saab adds that kinked braided hoses do not recover their shape. Audi (Q7 TDI) found moisture in sensor G505, Chrysler (2.8 diesel) checked sensor and connector, and Stellantis found open circuits and bad PCM grounds. Without a valid signal the soot load is estimated, often followed by P2463.

causes.label: Sensor hose disconnected, split, kinked or blocked
Sensor skewed or stuck, for example from moisture ingress
High resistance in sensor wiring or ECM grounds

symptoms: DPF warning, regeneration inhibited or too frequent

P2454.title: Diesel Particulate Filter Pressure Sensor A Circuit Low
P2454.description: The particulate filter pressure sensor is a three-wire part: the ECM feeds it 5 V and ground and reads a signal that rises with the pressure difference across the filter. P2454 means that signal sits below the lowest plausible value. Ford's 2023 diesels fail below 0.10 V within 2 s, where 0.45 V corresponds to zero pressure difference; GM's 2018 diesels fail below 3 % of the supply with 80 of 160 samples. On the Opel/GM 2.0 CDTi in the Saab 9-5 (2010) an open circuit sets P2454 as well as a short to ground, after 2 s, so a disconnected plug reads low there. A shorted 5 V reference can also pull the signal down and usually sets P0641 alongside. Audi (Q7 TDI 2009 to 2011) saw P2454 from moisture inside sensor G505, and Chrysler lists it on the 2.8 diesel Town and Country with a sensor and connector check. Without the signal the filter load is estimated and regeneration may be limited.

causes.label: Signal wire open or shorted to ground, connector unplugged
Internal sensor failure, for example from moisture
5 V reference shorted by another sensor on the same supply

P2455.title: Diesel Particulate Filter Pressure Sensor A Circuit High
P2455.description: P2455 means the particulate filter pressure sensor signal sits above the highest plausible value, at the top of the 5 V range. Ford's 2023 diesels and the Opel/GM 2.0 CDTi in the Saab 9-5 (2010) both use 4.9 V as the limit, Ford within 2 s and Saab after 1 s; on Ford's 6.7 L the signal follows roughly 0.082 V per kPa above 0.45 V, so 4.9 V would be about 54 kPa. Typical faults are a signal wire shorted to the 5 V reference or to battery voltage, or an open low-reference (ground) circuit, which Saab lists among the circuit faults for this code. A real pressure that high from a blocked filter is unusual and would normally first raise soot codes such as P2463. Chrysler lists P2455 on the 2.8 diesel Town and Country with a sensor and connector check. The ECM falls back to a modelled soot load and may limit regeneration.

causes.label: Signal wire shorted to 5 V reference or battery voltage

P2456.title: DPF Differential Pressure Sensor Circuit Intermittent
P2456.description: The DPF differential-pressure sensor delivers an intermittent signal — usually a marginal connector or a chafed wiring section that breaks contact during temperature or vibration.
symptoms: Check engine light or DPF warning light on

P2457.title: EGR Cooler Performance
P2457.description: The EGR cooler does not lower exhaust gas temperature as expected — typically internal coolant fouling, a partial blockage, or a cracked cooler that mixes coolant with exhaust gas.

P2458.title: Diesel Particulate Filter Regeneration Duration
P2458.description: During a regeneration the engine raises exhaust temperature, mostly by late post-injection burned in the oxidation catalyst, until the soot in the particulate filter oxidises. P2458 means a regeneration took longer than the calibrated limit, so the filter was not cleaned in the expected time. CARB asks diesel OBD to detect regenerations that do not complete as intended. On the Opel/GM 2.0 CDTi in the Saab 9-5 (2010) the ECM runs the check with coolant at 73 to 96 °C and sets the code when regeneration times are too long; it is a Type C code there, stored without the MIL. Volkswagen saw P2458 with the MIL on 2011 Jetta and Golf 2.0 TDI (CJAA) and fixed it with an ECM software update, so the calibration is worth checking before parts are replaced. Otherwise the regeneration is slowed by low exhaust temperature, a weak oxidation catalyst, faulty temperature or pressure readings, or trips too short to finish. P2459 covers regenerations that happen too often.

causes.label: ECM calibration that needs an update (documented by Volkswagen)
Short trips that keep regenerations from finishing
Oxidation catalyst too weak to reach regeneration temperature

symptoms: DPF warning or MIL, depending on the manufacturer
Cooling fan and raised idle running on after shutdown

P2459.title: Diesel Particulate Filter Regeneration Frequency
P2459.description: P2459 means the particulate filter is being regenerated more often than the calibration expects. CARB requires diesel OBD to flag regeneration so frequent that emissions would exceed the limit; frequent regeneration also dilutes oil and costs fuel. Ford's 2023 diesels set it when the average distance between completed regenerations falls below about 40 km. GM's 2014 Cruze 2.0 diesel compares the soot load that triggered a regeneration with a table built from the engine-out soot model, and GM's 2018 diesels flag a ratio of 10 or more between the pressure-based soot estimate and the engine-out model, citing dirty combustion, a leak in the intake or exhaust, or an inefficient filter. The Opel/GM 2.0 CDTi in the Saab 9-5 (2010) instead counts too many interrupted regenerations, as a Type C code. Stellantis replaced the filter on 2022 to 2023 Ram 2500/3500 6.7 Cummins over a manufacturing issue; left alone, the engine eventually derates.

causes.label: High soot output from the engine (injectors, EGR, air leaks)
Differential pressure reading too high (sensor, blocked or swapped hoses)
Filter loaded with ash or defective from manufacture

symptoms: Higher fuel consumption and rising oil level
Reduced engine power if the fault persists

P2463.title: Diesel Particulate Filter Restriction - Soot Accumulation (Bank 1)
P2463.description: P2463 means the soot load in the particulate filter has passed the level at which the engine still regenerates it on its own. GM's 2009 Duramax sets it at 70 g or more for 5 minutes, the 2014 Cruze 2.0 diesel at more than 32 g for 30 s, both as Type A codes; GM's 2018 diesels use the pressure-based soot model with 120 failures in 150 samples. On the Cruze the ECM then turns on the MIL, reduces engine power and blocks normal regeneration, so a dealer service regeneration is needed. GM's bulletin on the related driver messages notes that the filter cleans itself about once per tank and needs driving above 50 km/h; extended idling and stop-and-go traffic keep it from finishing. The underlying cause is not always the driving: Stellantis traced P2463 with P2453 to broken differential pressure sensor wiring and PCM grounds, Mack to a failed aftertreatment fuel doser. Check those before regenerating, or the code returns.

Fault that prevents regeneration (fuel doser, temperature sensor)

P24E5.title: NH3 Sensor Circuit Intermittent/Erratic
P24E5.description: The ammonia (NH3) slip sensor downstream of the SCR catalyst delivers an intermittent or erratic signal. Used to close-loop the AdBlue/DEF dosing strategy.

causes.label: Chafed or vibrating harness near the exhaust

P24E6.title: NH3 Sensor Heater Circuit/Open
P24E6.description: The heater inside the ammonia (NH3) slip sensor warms the sensing cell to operating temperature so it can read tailpipe ammonia. The ECM detects an open in the heater control circuit — no current flows when the heater should be active, so the sensor never reaches its working point and SCR closed-loop control is suspended.

causes.label: Burnt-out heater winding inside the sensor
Failed heater driver stage in the dosing module

P24E7.title: NH3 Sensor Heater Circuit Low
P24E7.description: The heater control circuit of the ammonia (NH3) slip sensor reads below the expected voltage range. Either the wiring is shorted to ground or the heater driver in the SCR/dosing module is stuck low. The sensor element never warms up, NH3 readings stay invalid and the SCR strategy falls back to open-loop dosing.

causes.label: Heater control wire shorted to ground
Internal short across the heater element
Low-side driver pulled down in the control module

P24E8.title: NH3 Sensor Heater Circuit High
P24E8.description: The heater control circuit of the NH3 slip sensor reads above the expected voltage range. Typically a short to battery voltage or a heater driver stuck high — duty-cycle control is lost, the heater either runs continuously or not at all, and the sensor element risks overheating before the ECM disables it.

causes.label: Heater control wire shorted to battery voltage
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P24E9.title: NH3 Sensor Heater Circuit Performance

P24EA.title: NH3 Sensor Supply Voltage Circuit

causes.label: High-resistance ground at the SCR module

P24EC.title: NH3 Sensor Supply Voltage Circuit High

causes.label: Supply line shorted to battery voltage

P24ED.title: NH3 Sensor Calibration Memory

Without the trim values the raw ammonia reading is unreliable.

causes.label: New sensor installed but not coded/learned to the ECM
Corrupted calibration memory after voltage drop
Module software outdated, reflash may resolve

P24EE.title: NH3 Sensor Processor Performance

The sensor cannot guarantee its output value, the ECM marks the channel invalid and disables SCR closed-loop control on this branch.

causes.label: Module software outdated, reflash may resolve

Without it, the module either fails to wake up at start-up or stays awake and drains the battery.

causes.label: Broken wake-up wire or unplugged connector

P24F0.title: Control Module Wake-up Circuit Low
P24F0.description: The wake-up input on the control module reads stuck low — usually a short to ground or a permanently asserted wake signal. The module either keeps waking up unnecessarily and drains the battery, or it cannot distinguish a real wake event from the stuck low level.

causes.label: Door, hood or terminal switch stuck closed
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P24F1.title: Control Module Wake-up Circuit High
P24F1.description: The wake-up input reads above the expected range — typically a short to battery voltage. The module sees a permanent wake-up request, never enters sleep mode and drains the battery while parked.

causes.label: Wake-up wire shorted to battery voltage
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
Supply wire pinched against B+ source

P24F2.title: EGR Temperature/Charge Air Cooler Temperature Correlation
P24F2.description: After a long key-off soak both the EGR temperature sensor and the charge-air cooler outlet temperature sensor must read approximately the same ambient temperature. The ECM compares them and detects an implausible delta. One of the sensors drifts, is wired wrong, or is exposed to a heat source the model does not know about.

causes.label: Residual heat in the charge-air cooler after a hot soak

P24F3.title: Reductant Tank Temperature/Fuel Temperature Correlation
P24F3.description: After a long key-off soak the AdBlue/DEF tank temperature and the fuel tank temperature should read close to each other (both at ambient). The ECM detects an implausible spread, which usually means one of the two sensors drifts, is wired wrong, or has a heat source nearby that the plausibility model does not account for.

causes.label: One temperature sensor drifting outside tolerance
Recently active reductant tank heater warming the tank above ambient

symptoms: Check engine light or NOx warning on
Possible no-start countdown after ignore period

P24F4.title: NOx Sensor Delayed Response - High to Low Bank 1 Sensor 1
P24F4.description: The pre-catalyst NOx sensor on bank 1 (sensor 1) reacts too slowly when NOx in the exhaust drops from a high to a low level — for example after a fuel cut or transition into low-load. Aged ceramic cells, soot deposits or condensation inside the sensor protective tube slow the diffusion of NOx to the measuring element.

causes.label: Aged sensor element with reduced response speed

symptoms: Check engine light or NOx warning on
Possible no-start countdown after ignore period

P24F5.title: NOx Sensor Delayed Response - High to Low Bank 1 Sensor 2
P24F5.description: The post-catalyst NOx sensor on bank 1 (sensor 2) reacts too slowly when NOx in the exhaust drops from a high to a low level. Same failure mechanism as the upstream sensor — aged element, soot or condensate — but post-catalyst the consequence is a degraded SCR conversion-efficiency monitor.

causes.label: Aged sensor element with reduced response speed

symptoms: Check engine light or NOx warning on
Possible no-start countdown after ignore period

P24F6.title: Exhaust Aftertreatment Fuel Air Purge Valve Stuck Open
P24F6.description: On systems that inject HC dosing fuel or AIR-assisted reductant into the aftertreatment, a purge valve clears the line after each dosing event. The ECM detects the valve stuck open — pressure or flow does not build up against a closed valve, so the dosing line cannot be charged. Common on diesel HC-doser hardware (DPF regen support).

causes.label: Mechanically stuck open valve from soot or coking
Carbon or debris buildup preventing free movement

P24F7.title: Exhaust Aftertreatment Fuel Air Purge Valve Stuck Closed
P24F7.description: The aftertreatment HC dosing or reductant purge valve is stuck closed. The ECM commands purge but the line is not cleared, leaving residual fluid that can foul nozzles or freeze in cold weather. Subsequent dosing events also fail because backpressure does not match the model.

causes.label: Stuck closed by deposits or seized armature
Carbon or debris buildup preventing free movement

P24F8.title: Exhaust Aftertreatment Fuel Air Purge Valve Control Circuit
P24F8.description: General electrical fault in the control circuit of the aftertreatment fuel/air purge valve. The ECM cannot drive the valve coil according to plausibility checks — open, short or unexpected feedback voltage. Until cleared, dosing line purge is suspended.

causes.label: Failed driver stage in the dosing module

P24F9.title: Exhaust Aftertreatment Fuel Air Purge Valve Control Circuit Range/Performance
P24F9.description: The valve coil is electrically intact, but the response (current rise time, return-current decay, position feedback) does not match the ECM model. Typical for solenoids losing magnetic strength after long thermal cycling, or armatures with increased friction from coking.

causes.label: Aged solenoid with weakened magnetic force
Sensor element aged beyond calibration window

P24FA.title: Exhaust Aftertreatment Fuel Air Purge Valve Control Circuit Low
P24FA.description: The control circuit of the aftertreatment purge valve reads stuck low — usually a short to ground or a failed low-side driver. The valve is energised continuously when it should be off, or the diagnostic feedback voltage is pulled below threshold.

causes.label: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P24FB.title: Exhaust Aftertreatment Fuel Air Purge Valve Control Circuit High
P24FB.description: The control circuit of the aftertreatment purge valve reads stuck high — typically a short to battery voltage or an open ground/return path. The driver cannot pull the line low to actuate the valve.

causes.label: Control wire shorted to battery voltage
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P24FC.title: Particulate Matter Sensor Heater Control Circuit Driver Current/Temperature Too High
P24FC.description: The PM (soot) sensor heater is driven by a current-limited stage so it can burn off accumulated soot before each measurement. The driver reports current or junction temperature above the safe limit and disables itself. Often a partial short across the heater or sensor element after coolant intrusion.

causes.label: Partial short across the heater element
Driver overheating due to poor cooling on the module

P24FD.title: Particulate Filter A Incorrect
P24FD.description: The ECM identifies the installed particulate filter A as the wrong part — backpressure signature, regeneration efficiency or coded part-number do not match the application. Common after a non-OEM aftermarket DPF or a wrong-application replacement.
symptoms: Check engine light or DPF warning light on

P24FE.title: SCR Catalyst Incorrect
P24FE.description: The ECM identifies the installed SCR catalyst as the wrong part — NOx conversion efficiency, NH3 storage capacity or coded part-number do not match the expected application. Typical after fitting a non-OEM SCR brick or after a coding error following replacement.

causes.label: Incorrect or non-OEM SCR catalyst installed

symptoms: Sulfur (rotten egg) smell from exhaust under load

P24FF.title: Reductant Temperature Too High
P24FF.description: The temperature of the AdBlue/DEF in the dosing system exceeds the safe limit — risk of thermal decomposition (NH3/biuret formation) and clogged dosing nozzles. Often caused by a stuck-on tank heater, a stalled coolant return or proximity to a hot exhaust component.

causes.label: Heat soak from exhaust or engine bay

symptoms: Check engine light or NOx warning on
Possible no-start countdown after ignore period
